content_sections.heading: Kerala High Court Office Attendant Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: Vacancies arising during the validity period of the ranked list may also be filled from the same list. The ranked list will remain valid for a minimum period of one year from the date it comes into force. It may continue until a fresh ranked list is published or for a maximum period of two years, whichever is earlier.

content_sections.heading: Kerala High Court Office Attendant Qualification 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates applying for the Office Attendant post must satisfy both of the following educational conditions: Must have passed SSLC or an equivalent examination. Must not have acquired a graduation degree. All prescribed qualifications must be acquired on or before 26 October 2026, the closing date for submitting the online application. Candidates claiming an equivalent qualification must produce the relevant government order whenever requested by the High Court. Important: Candidates who have completed graduation are not eligible for the Kerala High Court Office Attendant post. Candidates shortlisted for the interview must submit an affidavit confirming that they had not acquired graduation as of the application closing date.

content_sections.heading: Kerala High Court Office Attendant Salary 2026
Kerala High Court Office Attendant Application Fee
content_sections.text: Candidates can pay the application fee through debit card, credit card, net banking or UPI. An offline payment option using the system-generated fee payment challan is also available. Applicable bank transaction charges must be paid by the candidate. Payments through demand draft, cheque, money order or postal order will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Kerala High Court Office Attendant Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: The selection process consists of the following stages: Objective written test Interview Certificate verification The written test will be objective type, conducted through an OMR answer sheet. The examination will have a duration of 75 minutes and carry 100 marks. Each correct answer carries one mark. One-fourth mark will be deducted for every incorrect answer. The written test will be bilingual in English and Malayalam. The written test duration is 75 minutes. The interview will carry 10 marks. Candidates must obtain at least 35% marks in the interview to be considered for inclusion in the ranked list. The number of candidates shortlisted for the interview will be decided by the High Court based on the notified vacancies, appointments made from the previous list and the possibility of additional vacancies.

content_sections.heading: Kerala High Court Office Attendant Exam Centres
content_sections.text: The written examination is proposed to be conducted at the following centres: Thiruvananthapuram Alappuzha Ernakulam Thrissur Kozhikode Candidates must select their preferred examination centre while completing the online application. Requests to change the selected examination centre will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Reservation for Differently Abled Candidates
content_sections.text: Four percent of Office Attendant vacancies will be reserved for eligible differently abled candidates in accordance with the applicable rules. The notification identifies the following suitable benchmark disability categories: Blindness and low vision Deaf and hard of hearing Specified locomotor disabilities Autism spectrum disorder in the specified categories Mild intellectual disability Specific learning disability Mental illness within the prescribed percentage Multiple disabilities involving the specified combinations The minimum functional requirements prescribed for the post include sitting, standing, walking, manipulation by fingers and seeing.

content_sections.heading: Scribe and Compensatory Time
content_sections.text: Differently abled candidates whose writing speed is affected may request a scribe while submitting the online application. The request for a scribe must be selected during the online application process. The qualification of the scribe must be one level below the minimum qualification prescribed for the post. The candidate must produce the prescribed medical certificate and declaration at the time of the examination. Eligible candidates may receive 25 minutes of compensatory time upon producing the required medical certificate.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for Kerala High Court Office Attendant Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Visit the Kerala High Court recruitment portal at hckrecruitment.keralacourts.in . Open the One Time Registration Login section. Complete the One Time Registration process if you are a new applicant. Sign in using the registered login details. Complete the required information under My Profile. Open the Dashboard and click Apply Now for Office Attendant Recruitment No. 21/2026. Enter the required personal, educational, community and other details. Upload the prescribed photograph and signature. Preview the application and verify all entered information. Submit the online application. Pay the application fee, if applicable. Download and print the submitted application for future reference. Important: Candidates do not need to send the printed application or supporting documents to the High Court. Once the application is submitted, editing or modification will not be permitted.

content_sections.heading: Photograph and Signature Requirements
content_sections.text: Candidates should keep scanned copies of their photograph and signature ready before beginning the online application. The photograph must be recent and passport size. The face and shoulders should be clearly visible. The face must be centrally focused. The photograph should have a white or light-coloured background. Candidates should follow the detailed photograph and signature guidelines available on the recruitment portal.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required
content_sections.text: Candidates must produce the applicable original documents whenever called by the High Court: SSLC certificate or equivalent qualification certificate Date of birth proof Community or caste certificate, if applicable Non-Creamy Layer certificate, if applicable Economically Weaker Section certificate, if applicable Benchmark disability certificate, if applicable Job-oriented physical and functionality certificate, if applicable No Objection Certificate or service certificate for government employees Government order proving equivalent qualification, if applicable Affidavit confirming that the candidate has not acquired graduation Valid identity proof Other certificates requested by the High Court

content_sections.heading: Kerala High Court Office Attendant Admission Ticket
content_sections.text: The admission ticket for the written test will be available approximately three weeks before the examination. Interview call letters will be available approximately two weeks before the interview. Candidates must log in to their profile on the Kerala High Court recruitment portal to download the admission ticket or call letter. Information regarding availability will also be sent through SMS or email.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: Only online applications submitted through the official recruitment portal will be accepted. Candidates must have acquired the required qualification by 26 October 2026. Graduates are not eligible for the Office Attendant post. The information entered in the online application must be complete and accurate. Applications without successful fee payment, where applicable, will be treated as incomplete. Government employees must obtain a No Objection Certificate or service certificate. Original certificates must be produced whenever requested by the High Court. Canvassing or providing false information will result in cancellation of candidature. Candidates should regularly check the official recruitment portal for examination and interview updates.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are available in Kerala High Court Office Attendant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The Kerala High Court has announced 17 anticipated Office Attendant vacancies.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: The last date to submit the online application and pay the fee through online mode is 26 October 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification required for Kerala High Court Office Attendant?
faq.answer: Candidates must have passed SSLC or an equivalent examination and must not have acquired graduation.

faq.question: Q4. Are graduates eligible to apply?
faq.answer: No. Candidates who have acquired graduation are not eligible for the Office Attendant post.

faq.question: Q5. What is the Kerala High Court Office Attendant salary?
faq.answer: The Office Attendant post carries a pay scale of Rs.23,000 to Rs.50,200.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: The application fee is Rs.500. Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and unemployed differently abled candidates are exempted from paying the fee.

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process?
faq.answer: Selection will be based on an objective written test, interview and certificate verification.

faq.question: Q8. Is there negative marking in the written test?
faq.answer: Yes. One-fourth mark will be deducted for every incorrect answer.

faq.question: Q9. What is the written examination duration?
faq.answer: The written examination will have a duration of 75 minutes.

faq.question: Q10. Can candidates apply offline?
faq.answer: No. Applications must be submitted online through the Kerala High Court recruitment portal.
